column7: λαλεῖν, 1Co 14:19 cf. 1Co 14:9. The plural in the phrase γλώσσαις λαλεῖν, used even of a single person (1Co 14:5f), refers to the various motions of the tongue. By metonymy, of the cause for the effect, γλῶσσαι tongues are equivalent to λόγοι ἐν γλώσσῃ (1Co 14:19) words spoken in a tongue (Zungenvorträge): 1Co 13:8; 1Co 14:22; γένη γλωσσῶν, 1Co 12:10, 1Co 12:28, of which two kinds are mentioned viz. προσευχή and ψαλμός, 1Co 14:15; γλῶσσαν ἔχω, something to utter with a tongue, 1Co 14:26. (On 'Speaking with Tongues' see, in addition to the discussions above referred to, Wendt in the 5th edition of Meyer on Acts (Act 2:4); Heinrici, Korinthierbriefe, i., 372ff; Schaff, Hist. of the Chr. Church, i. 234-245 (1882); Farrar, St. Paul, i. 95ff.)
